methodological_rigor.justification: The study develops DKK1-A2 (HLA-A*0201/DKK1-P20 peptide complex) CAR-T cells using a murine C2 antibody scFv and a humanized hC2 version, with CD8a hinge/4-1BB/CD3zeta/eGFP architecture. In vitro validation includes cytotoxicity (luciferase and flow cytometry), proliferation (CellTrace), cytokine secretion (intracellular staining + ELISA) across MM, PDAC, NSCLC, and TNBC lines, DKK1-KO JeKo-1 specificity controls, and HLA-A2-transduced derivatives. In vivo work spans multiple xenograft models (U266, KMS-26, KMS-12-BM, MM.1S MM; CFPAC-1, PANC-1 PDAC subcutaneous and orthotopic; NCI-H441 NSCLC metastatic; MDA-MB-231 TNBC orthotopic and subcutaneous), a PDAC PDX from 7 patients (with DKK1-A2 CAR-T efficacy in HLA-A2+ patient #1), and tumor rechallenge experiments. Safety includes hDKK1-A2 transgenic mice (human DKK1 + HLA-A2 transgenic), in vitro CRS tripartite coculture, and an in vivo CRS model. Statistical approach uses t-tests, ANOVA, log-rank, and simple linear regression without explicit multiplicity correction across many outcomes. Sample sizes per group are typically n=4-5, limiting power to detect subtle safety signals.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical CAR-T development spanning cell lines, multiple xenograft models, PDX, and safety-oriented transgenic mice; Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is high because solid-tumor CAR-T is a major unmet need, DKK1 is broadly expressed across MM and multiple solid tumors with limited normal-tissue expression (except placenta/testis/tonsil), and HLA-A*0201 occurs in 30-50% of the population. The DKK1-A2 peptide-MHC CAR approach (pHLA-CAR) parallels ongoing clinical programs and could enter IND development directly.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies. IRB and IACUC approvals at Houston Methodist are stated, maximal tumor burden criteria are defined (hind limb paralysis for MM; 20 mm diameter for solid tumors), sex-balanced mouse usage (6-8 weeks, both sexes) is noted, and a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced. Per-experiment sample sizes are given in figure legends (n=4-5 biological replicates). Randomization, blinding, and explicit power calculations are not documented. Source Data files are referenced for all figures. Specific databases (GEPIA2, GSE13591, GSE2350, GSE13159, GSE16515, GSE10072, EGAS00000000083) are cited for public analyses; deposition of any newly generated sequencing data is not indicated because this is primarily a cell/animal therapeutics paper.

novelty_literature.justification: This is, to the paper's framing, the first CAR-T cell against the DKK1-A2 peptide-MHC complex. Prior work included the C2 TCR-like antibody (ref 28) and DKK1-based vaccines/antibodies; the CAR-T format and the demonstration of efficacy across multiple hematologic and solid tumor models (MM, PDAC, NSCLC, TNBC) within one platform is a meaningful extension. pHLA-CAR is an active but crowded space (e.g., WT1-A2, PRAME-A2 programs); the DKK1-A2 target specificity, including the humanized hC2 version with a central memory bias and superior in vivo persistence, is a notable advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with logical progression from antigen characterization to CAR design, in vitro potency, in vivo efficacy across tumor types, PDX, humanization, memory phenotype, and safety testing. Figures are cited systematically. Minor grammatical issues are present but do not impede comprehension. Tables are not extensive but cell-line/xenograft parameters are described in text.

key_strengths: First DKK1-A2 pHLA-CAR demonstrating efficacy across MM (U266, KMS-26, KMS-12-BM, MM.1S), PDAC (CFPAC-1, PANC-1, PDX from HLA-A2+ patient #1), NSCLC (NCI-H441 metastatic), and TNBC (MDA-MB-231 orthotopic) xenografts
Antigen-specificity established through DKK1-KO JeKo-1 controls and HLA-A2-transduced derivatives; no reactivity to HLA-A2+ healthy donor blood/bone marrow
Humanized hC2 CAR-T cells show central memory phenotype (CCR7+CD45RO+, ~70%) with superior in vivo persistence and rechallenge protection
Safety-oriented hDKK1/HLA-A2 double transgenic mice and CRS in vitro/in vivo models with no detectable toxicity
key_concerns: Safety testing relies on a constructed transgenic model and limited xenograft cohorts; on-target/off-tumor risks in placenta/testis/tonsil are not fully addressed in transgenic tissue
Per-group sample sizes (n=4-5) and absence of formal multiplicity correction across many parallel comparisons limit statistical robustness
PDX efficacy is demonstrated in only one HLA-A2+ PDAC patient (#1); broader PDX panel would strengthen claims
Randomization and blinding procedures for in vivo tumor measurements are not described
chief_reviewer.rationale: A comprehensive preclinical CAR-T package targeting a peptide-MHC with broad applicability and humanized construct ready for IND; top-tier plausible (e.g., Nature Cancer) with minor revisions on on-target/off-tumor safety and statistical rigor.
